newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi to deport 46 Indian children for begging.
newsitem.headline: Saudi to deport 46 Indian children for begging.

text.p: Saudi Arabia will soon deport 46 children aged between six and 14, many apparently used as beggars by parents, Indian diplomats in the kingdom said on Saturday.

The 40 boys and six girls were caught by authorities while asking for food and money in the streets of the cities of Mecca and Medina hosting two of Islam's holiest shrines and were taken to the deportation centre in nearby Jeddah last week.
Many of them appeared to have entered Saudi - known for its strict visa laws, as Moslem pilgrims accompanying their family, who would return to India leaving them behind, they explained.

They would be the second batch of Indian children to be deported from Saudi Arabia in less than two weeks for overstaying illegally in the oil-rich country and earning their living as beggars. At least 76 girls aged between five and 14, many handicapped, were deported to Bombay on January 13.

Diplomats in the Indian consulate in Western city of Jeddah on the Red Sea coast visited the children in the deportation centre after Saudi authorities contacted them last week. They had no official identification papers with them.

"After talking to them and satisfying ourselves that they are Indians, the consulate started the process of issuing them with travel documents, the first step towards deportation...," one diplomat told Reuters by telephone from Saudi Arabia.
"We hope this process will be completed today (Saturday), or tomorrow (Sunday) and after that, past experience shows they will be deported in a week or so."
Saudi Arabia, which is providing them with food and other basic needs, will also pay for their return air tickets.
Most of them hail from Murshidbad in India's eastern state of West Bengal.
Diplomats said Indian authorities have been investigating the matter in great detail since the first group returned.
"Until investigations are over things cannot be fully determined," one said. "But our suspicion is that there is an organised ring behind it."
